races.name: Wyvis Roofing EBF Maiden Stakes (Hamilton Park 2yo Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Carrow Road
runners_data.comment: £40,000 breeze-up 2yo; half-brother to two winners; market should be revealing
runners_data.spotlight: 17,000gns yearling, £40,000 breeze-up 2yo; by Caturra; fifth foal; half-brother to winners Manila Scouse (5f/6f including 2yo; RPR 95) and Tasever (7f/1m AW; 76); dam well held in two runs but from a good family; stable not associated with winning 2yo newcomers but he's bred to be sharp and is worth a market check.

runners_data.name: Sale Shark
runners_data.comment: 52,000gns yearling with seven winning siblings; yard's 2yos going well; a newcomer of note
runners_data.spotlight: 52,000euros yearling; tenth foal; closely related to 7f AW 2yo winner Jacinth (RPR 84), half-brother to six winners including Ekhtiyaar (Group-placed 6f including 2yo; 116), New Providence (5f/6f including 2yo/Group 3; 110) and Dick Datchery (6f including 2yo; 84); dam unplaced 1m-1m2f; stable's 2yos are going well and he is a newcomer of note.

runners_data.name: Or Another
runners_data.comment: Shaped with promise when 3rd at Pontefract last month; open to improvement; key player
runners_data.spotlight: Looked a big threat 1f out on his Pontefract debut four weeks ago (5f, good) but was unable to sustain his effort; he should be more streetwise under pressure this time and he is a strong contender for his in-form stable.

runners_data.name: Jaijai
runners_data.comment: 6th of ten behind a smart prospect at Ascot (6f, good) 18 days ago; should be more to come
runners_data.spotlight: Weakened in the closing stages when sixth of ten in an Ascot novice (6f, good) 18 days ago; this looks easier and although he is bred to need further, he's still of serious interest.

runners_data.name: Rbflying
runners_data.comment: Dropped right out when 6th at Thirsk 47 days ago; needs to leave that well behind
runners_data.spotlight: Dropped away to finish sixth of the eight runners, beaten 12l, in a 5f maiden (good ground) at Thirsk 47 days ago; needs to leave that run well behind to feature.

runners_data.name: North Star Kodi
runners_data.comment: Green when 3rd over 6f here 12 days ago; 2nd there has been well beaten since; 5f a query
runners_data.spotlight: In need of the experience when third in a 6f maiden here 12 days ago; should be more streetwise today but the runner-up in that race has been well beaten since and dropping to 5f isn't sure to suit.

races.name: One Stop Roofing Supplies Ltd Restricted Novice Stakes (For horses In Bands C And D) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Togeather Forever
runners_data.comment: Half-brother to four winners (three useful) but probably a longer-term prospect
runners_data.spotlight: Eleventh foal; half-brother to winners Ralston Road (1m2f-1m6f including Listed; RPR 110), Carbon Dating (1m3f-1m6f; 110), Wickywickywheels (1m3f-1m5f including UAE Listed; 104) and Krissy (1m1f-1m4f; 76); dam unraced; should have a future but perhaps further down the line; hooded for debut.

runners_data.name: Lavatera
runners_data.comment: 17,000gns yearling; dam a sister to 1000 Guineas third Moth; trainer also runs Alterity
runners_data.spotlight: 6,000gns yearling, resold 17,000gns yearling; sixth foal; dam once-raced (RPR 69) sister to 7f winner/1,000 Guineas third Moth and 12.5f Listed winner Dirgam, half-sister to 1m2f Group 3 winner Hearthstead Maison; trainer is also responsible for Alterity.

runners_data.name: Pepsea
runners_data.comment: Second to Bearish on last month's Thirsk debut (1m); 7lb better off for 0.75l today
runners_data.spotlight: Enjoyed the run of the race when second of six on his Thirsk debut (1m, good) 47 days ago, unable to fend off Bearish's late thrust; 7lb better off with his old rival and could take a step forward.

runners_data.name: Bearish
runners_data.comment: Beat Pepsea at Thirsk on last month's reappearance; 2yo debut form was even better
runners_data.spotlight: Didn't have to match the form of last year's promising debut at Newmarket to see off Pepsea and four others at Thirsk last month; 7lb worse off with Pepsea today but may still uphold the placings; the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Ice Show
runners_data.comment: In need of the experience when fifth at Newcastle last month (1m); should do better
runners_data.spotlight: In need of the experience when fifth of 12 at Newcastle (1m) on last month's debut; can do better but such progress is essential; trainer also runs Sogniamo.

runners_data.name: Alterity
runners_data.comment: Smart pedigree; last summer's Newmarket debut wasn't without hope; can do better this year
runners_data.spotlight: Well-bred filly; easy to back and ended up a well-beaten fifth of 12 at Newmarket on her debut last July (7f, good to soft); can leave that initial effort well behind her this year.

runners_data.name: Sogniamo
runners_data.comment: Well beaten in one run for Marcus Tregoning last summer (7f); bred to do much better
runners_data.spotlight: 25-1 and finished a well-beaten last of eight in one run for Marcus Tregoning last summer (7f, good to firm); today's trip more suitable and worth a market check starting out for a new stable (same owners).

races.name: ICB (Water Proofing) Handicap

runners_data.name: Tricky Tel
runners_data.note: Prominent runner ideally placed to track the pace battle and strike when leaders weaken
runners_data.comment: Two 2yo wins and his promising reappearance were all at Chester; can he deliver elsewhere?
runners_data.spotlight: Began his career with a pair of 5f wins at Chester last May; progress stalled last summer but he returned from a 223-day absence with a good run back at Chester three weeks ago, third of 12 in a 6f handicap on good ground (wide draw); looks on a good mark but can he deliver away from Chester?

runners_data.name: Back To Me
runners_data.note: Hold-up style perfectly suited to the strong early pace that three leaders will create
runners_data.comment: Unplaced in both turf starts but 2-2 on AW (6f/7f); drops back in trip; not yet exposed
runners_data.spotlight: 2-2 on AW, including a 7f novice at Southwell on his stable debut in April; only midfield in a 7f handicap at Wetherby three weeks later; drops back in trip with further improvement possible.

runners_data.name: Sierra Sands
runners_data.note: Late-running style gives him excellent chances if the pace-setters burn each other out early
runners_data.comment: All races at 7f; reappearance was promising and can be given a pass for last time; chance
runners_data.spotlight: Promise as a 2yo, including a Catterick win (7f, good); not beaten far on his seasonal/handicap debut last month but he took a backwards step 25 days ago (reportedly lost action); drops to 6f for the first time and could still have a bigger run in him.

runners_data.name: Siouxpersonic
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare should benefit from the fierce gallop and can finish strongly under Sexton
runners_data.comment: Promising stable debut when second at Ripon last month (6f); up 3lb but commands respect
runners_data.spotlight: 5f AW win for Ed Bethell; good start for her new connections when a close second of ten at Ripon last month (6f, good; first two clear); up 3lb but she can't be ruled out.

runners_data.name: Falcon Queen
runners_data.note: Huge drop in class from Irish maidens and light weight could spring a surprise at big odds
runners_data.comment: Similar form in three Dundalk maidens for K Condon; sold 22,000gns since latest; unexposed
runners_data.spotlight: Similar form when finishing fourth in three Dundalk maidens (5f-7f) for K J Condon; sold for 22,000gns last month; open to further progress now handicapping.

runners_data.name: March Ahead
runners_data.note: Long absence of 222 days is a major concern despite his front-running style suiting the track layout
runners_data.comment: 6f novice win before unplaced in two nurseries last year; new yard; tough mark
runners_data.spotlight: Made all to win a Carlisle fillies' novice (6f, good to firm) last summer when trained by Kevin Ryan; the handicapper looked in charge in two nurseries in the autumn and she may need a bit more weight off her back; first run for Bryan Smart (same owner).

runners_data.name: Watchdog
runners_data.note: Recent winner but another 5lb rise makes life tougher against this stronger field
runners_data.comment: Progressed well since December; rises in class here but another bold bid is expected
runners_data.spotlight: Ended 2025 with a pair of Class 6 wins on AW (7f/6f); his progress has continued back on turf, making all in 6f handicaps at Redcar and Doncaster; another 5lb higher today and also steps up into a Class 4 but he is still more appealing than many.

runners_data.name: Douwantitrightnow
runners_data.note: Front-runner returning after 107-day break with poor recent form trend suggesting vulnerability
runners_data.comment: 33-1 when last of four on her handicap debut; down in trip with a point to prove
runners_data.spotlight: Her third 2yo run represented a jolt of improvement but she failed to build on it when last of four on her handicap debut in February (33-1); a 1lb drop in the weights is not enough to tempt this time.

races.paceDynamic: Watchdog, March Ahead and Douwantitrightnow will lead from the gates in this 6f handicap, creating a fierce early gallop with three confirmed front-runners committed to making the running. The relentless pace will string out the field and test stamina reserves over this sharp track. With the pace-setters likely to burn each other out, the strong pace will set up perfectly for the hold-up horses who can finish fastest. This race shape strongly favours the late-running brigade who can exploit the inevitable weakening of the pace-setters.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the three leaders go too hard early and weaken significantly in the final furlong
scenarios.body: The breakneck gallop will perfectly set up the closers who can unleash their finishing kicks. Sierra Sands, Back To Me and Siouxpersonic should have ideal conditions to strike late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Watchdog Survives Duel
scenarios.trigger: If Watchdog can break clear of his pace rivals and maintain his advantage to the line
scenarios.body: His recent winning form gives him the edge over March Ahead and Douwantitrightnow in the early battle. The 5lb rise may not stop his momentum if he can get first run on his rivals.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tactical Win
scenarios.trigger: If Tricky Tel tracks the pace perfectly and strikes at the ideal moment
scenarios.body: The Hugo Palmer runner can sit just behind the speed duel and pounce when the leaders tire. His prominent style gives him the tactical edge between the all-out pacers and deep closers.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Springs Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and allows a rank outsider to steal through late
scenarios.body: Falcon Queen or a well-positioned runner could benefit from complete chaos up front. The light weights and trainer changes add unpredictability to the mix.

watchPoints.text: March Ahead could be ring-rusty after 222 days off despite being a confirmed pace-setter in this speed battle
Watchdog faces his biggest test yet with a 5lb rise and stronger opposition than his recent Class 6 wins
Sierra Sands showed backwards step last time but the return to 6f could reignite his form
Back To Me drops back in trip from 7f to 6f which may not suit his stamina-laden profile
Falcon Queen represents significant class relief after three Irish maiden fourths at Dundalk

races.name: Cupa Slates Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Raulin
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse faces tactical disadvantage with limited pace, but David Nolan's experience and 4lb drop in handicap mark provide hope
runners_data.comment: On a good mark and dropping in grade but he has to prove his stamina for 1m5f
runners_data.spotlight: Three wins over 1m2f last season; unplaced twice this year but dropped 4lb for his troubles and this represents an ease in grade; stamina for 1m5f not assured.

runners_data.name: Shipshape
runners_data.note: Prominent runner perfectly suited to race shape, Connor Beasley has ridden him to good effect recently over extended distances
runners_data.comment: Improving as his stamina is drawn out; should give it another good shot
runners_data.spotlight: Running well since upped to 1m6f, recording form figures of 212 on his last three starts; no obvious reason he wouldn't go well again and he is travelling a long way for this assignment.

runners_data.name: Gentle Warrior
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse but has shown ability to race prominently, headgear change with visor suggests connections seeking improvement
runners_data.comment: Two wins at around 1m6f last September; second (of 4) last time; shouldn't be too far away
runners_data.spotlight: Won twice over about 1m6f last September; low-key seasonal return last month but he fared better, albeit beaten at a short price, at Nottingham 18 days ago; shouldn't be too far away.

runners_data.name: Ludo's Landing
runners_data.note: Natural front runner gets ideal scenario with no pace pressure, but two poor runs since March win raise questions about current form
runners_data.comment: Two disappointing runs have followed March's Class 5 success; has run well here before
runners_data.spotlight: Dipped into Class 5 company at Newcastle in March and won comfortably (extended 1m4f); two disappointing runs have followed and he now has a point to prove; has run well in two course visits, at least.

runners_data.name: Furhaan
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse needs everything to fall right, but Lauren Young's 5lb claim and quick return after 10 days might indicate readiness
runners_data.comment: On a winning mark but his success was on heavy and he is yet to shine for Jim Goldie
runners_data.spotlight: Made a winning handicap debut for Ed Walker off this mark last September (extended 1m3f, heavy); well short of that level in three runs for his new connections and he could prove vulnerable again.

races.paceDynamic: Ludo's Landing looks the only confirmed front runner in this small field, likely to take them along at a steady gallop without pressure from the gate. Shipshape and potentially Gentle Warrior will sit prominent behind the leader, while Raulin and Furhaan are hold-up horses who need the race to develop. With limited early pace and a sustainable tempo likely, this sets up perfectly for the prominent runners who can track Ludo's Landing and have first run on the stretched-out hold-up horses. This race shape strongly favours prominent/tracking horses who can position close to the pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Shipshape or Gentle Warrior track Ludo's Landing and get first run
scenarios.body: The steady pace allows prominent runners to conserve energy and kick when the hold-up horses are still struggling into contention. Shipshape's recent 1m6f form or Gentle Warrior's staying power proves decisive.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Ludo's Landing gets an uncontested lead and sustains his gallop
scenarios.body: The lack of early pressure allows him to dictate terms and his March win shows he retains ability when conditions suit. The hold-up horses leave their runs too late on the long straight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Times Run
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes truly crawling and Raulin gets a perfect ride from Nolan
scenarios.body: The slow tempo allows Raulin to use his class advantage and David Nolan's timing proves crucial in the finish. His three 1m2f wins last season suggest the stamina is there.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Surprise Furhaan Revival
scenarios.trigger: If Lauren Young can find a pocket trip and Furhaan rediscovers his September form
scenarios.body: The 5lb claim and light weight help, plus Jim Goldie's yard is in better form recently. His heavy ground win suggests more ability than recent runs indicate.

watchPoints.text: Ludo's Landing in the market - if well-supported despite recent poor form, connections clearly expect the return to front-running tactics to spark revival
Shipshape's early positioning - needs to track the leader closely rather than getting too far back given his prominent style works best
Gentle Warrior's headgear and early tactics - the visor suggests they want him sharper and more forward than his usual hold-up style
Raulin's price - any strong market confidence would be concerning given the tactical disadvantage his hold-up style faces here
Furhaan and Lauren Young's 5lb claim - watch for any positive signals from the Jim Goldie team about returning to winning form

races.name: David Hardie Engineering Ltd Handicap

runners_data.name: Vingegaard
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 35-day break with blinkers fitted, needs strong pace to be effective in small field
runners_data.comment: Best run for new connections when 3rd at Catterick five weeks ago; this demands even more
runners_data.spotlight: He ran his best race for current connections when third of five at Catterick five weeks ago (6f, good; blinkers first time); dropped 2lb but suspicion he will remain vulnerable.

runners_data.name: Tiva
runners_data.note: Proven at this trip with hold-up style but faces tactical disadvantage against likely weak pace scenario
runners_data.comment: Stiff tasks following back-to-back 5f wins last August; better expected today
runners_data.spotlight: Back-to-back 5f wins last August saw her soar up the weights; struggled in Listed company on her final two runs last year and she was again well held on her seasonal return at Ripon last month; down in class today and a better run is expected.

runners_data.name: Oriental Prince
runners_data.note: Prominent runner in good AW form returning to turf, strong trainer record and well-positioned tactically
runners_data.comment: In good form on AW over the winter; absent 131 days; fine on fast turf; not discounted
runners_data.spotlight: In good order on AW over the winter, going close off this mark twice following a Class 4 win in November; returning to turf not a bother and he can't be discounted.

runners_data.name: Binadham
runners_data.note: Gets 2lb pull with Law Of Average from last meeting where he finished close second, suits prominent tactics
runners_data.comment: Closely matched with Law Of Average on latest Bath run; should go well again
runners_data.spotlight: Good efforts on his last three starts, not quite able to peg back Law Of Average's advantage when second at Bath four weeks ago (5f, firm); 2lb better off today and he should give his running again.

runners_data.name: Law Of Average
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner in winning form who can control tempo, questionable head carriage adds slight concern
runners_data.comment: Fast front-runner when on song; can confirm Bath placings with Binadham; big chance
runners_data.spotlight: Progressive 3yo but his form headed south last year; back to winning ways when making all at Bath (5f, firm) four weeks ago; his head carriage has always been a bit ungainly but he's tough to pass when on song; major player despite the 4lb rise.

runners_data.name: Classy Al
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with course and distance wins but struggles with his racing manners and faces tactical disadvantage
runners_data.comment: Two C&D wins on his record; looks awkward but capable on his day; others safer this time
runners_data.spotlight: Does plenty wrong during his races but it hasn't stopped him from winning seven times, two of them over C&D; running himself back into form this year but others appeal more.

races.paceDynamic: Law Of Average will dominate from the front with Oriental Prince and Binadham providing some early company in prominent positions. The pace will be steady rather than fierce given only one confirmed front-runner and limited early pressure. This creates a scenario where Law Of Average can dictate terms through honest fractions without being harassed early. This race shape strongly favours front-runners and prominent racers who can track the pace, as hold-up horses like Vingegaard, Tiva and Classy Al will struggle to make up ground in a small field with limited pace collapse.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Law Of Average jumps well and faces minimal early pressure from the prominent runners
scenarios.body: He can control the tempo completely and prove hard to peg back in the straight with his recent winning form. The lack of sustained pace pressure plays directly into his hands having made all successfully last time.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Oriental Prince or Binadham can sit close enough to Law Of Average without being headed off early pace
scenarios.body: They get first run on the leader turning for home and can use their higher ratings to edge clear. Oriental Prince's AW form suggests he's ready to strike while Binadham was close to Law Of Average last time with worse terms.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold Up Success
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes surprisingly strong with Oriental Prince and Binadham both pressuring Law Of Average
scenarios.body: This creates enough pace collapse for Tiva to produce her finishing kick from the rear. Her back-to-back wins last August showed she has the class when conditions align.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Compromise Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Law Of Average fails to lead cleanly or gets headed early by one of the prominent runners
scenarios.body: The race becomes a messy tactical affair where any horse with tactical speed can capitalize. Vingegaard's third place last time suggests he might have more to offer in a truly-run race.

watchPoints.text: Law Of Average's head carriage and racing manners early - any signs of his old quirks could compromise his front-running advantage
Oriental Prince's jumping from the gates - if he misses the break he loses his key tactical position tracking the leader
Binadham's positioning in the first furlong - needs to be handy to use his 2lb advantage from their last meeting
Tiva's early movement - any sign of her being ridden more aggressively suggests connections expect stronger pace
The pace through the first two furlongs - if it's genuinely strong it completely changes the complexion for hold-up horses

races.name: Fixing Point Cladding Fasteners Handicap

runners_data.name: Light Dreamer
runners_data.note: Prominent runner gets ideal pace setup but 26 days off and needs to overcome disappointing recent efforts including poor Ascot showing.
runners_data.comment: Not built on debut promise yet but goes handicapping in an uncompetitive race
runners_data.spotlight: Unable to build on her debut promise in two runs since, albeit in the face of a still task at Ascot last time; makes her handicap debut in an uncompetitive race and she could have more to offer.

runners_data.name: Saxophonist
runners_data.note: Hold-up style faces pace disadvantage but solid Doncaster handicap third gives him proven form edge over rivals in similar company.
runners_data.comment: Doncaster 3rd last month looks solid form; open to improvement and he's the one to beat
runners_data.spotlight: Bettered his novice/maiden form when third of seven in a Doncaster handicap in April (1m, good to firm); that form looks solid and he remains capable of better.

runners_data.name: Porth Eilian
runners_data.note: Another hold-up runner with breeding appeal but must prove novice form translates to handicap company against these more experienced rivals.
runners_data.comment: Needs to improve for switch to handicaps but there are grounds for expecting much better
runners_data.spotlight: Half-sister to connections' smart Point Lynas; needs to step up on the form of her three runs in fillies' novice/maiden company but she may do just that.

races.paceDynamic: Light Dreamer will lead or race prominently from the start with minimal early pressure in this small field. Saxophonist and Porth Eilian both hold-up runners will track well off the pace, allowing Light Dreamer to dictate fractions through the middle stages. The lack of pace pressure means Light Dreamer can control the gallop and kick when ready, while the hold-up pair face the challenge of making up significant ground in the straight. This race shape strongly favours the front-running/prominent profile as Light Dreamer can steal a decisive advantage without being harassed for speed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Front Running
scenarios.trigger: If Light Dreamer gets soft early fractions and isn't pressed for pace.
scenarios.body: Light Dreamer controls the tempo throughout and has enough left to repel late challenges from Saxophonist and Porth Eilian. The hold-up pair struggle to bridge the gap having given the leader too much rope.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Strong Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Saxophonist produces his best form and gets a perfect hold-up trip.
scenarios.body: The pace becomes truly crawling allowing Saxophonist to unleash a devastating late kick that catches Light Dreamer flat-footed. His Doncaster third form proves reliable and superior class tells.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Surprise Improvement
scenarios.trigger: If Porth Eilian steps forward significantly from novice company into handicaps.
scenarios.body: The pace suits her hold-up style and the half-sister to Point Lynas shows hidden ability in this easier assignment. She picks up the pieces when the principals fail to deliver.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Light Dreamer goes too slow and stops dramatically in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The crawling pace suits nobody and all three finish in a heap with little separating them. Form becomes irrelevant in a messy finish.

watchPoints.text: Light Dreamer's early positioning - if she settles further back than usual the pace advantage disappears completely.
Saxophonist's market move - any significant support suggests connections expect the pace setup to suit despite tactical concerns.
Porth Eilian's jumping from the stalls - needs to be alert to avoid giving the leader an unassailable advantage.
Overall pace through the first half-mile - if genuinely crawling all three could finish in a blanket.
Light Dreamer's response to pressure in the straight - recent form suggests stamina/battling qualities are questionable.

races.name: Compass Roofing Handicap

runners_data.name: Donna Nook
runners_data.note: Prominent runner but 18-race losing streak is concerning, though showed ability when close second to Starliner at Ayr
runners_data.comment: On losing run and disappointed last time but her earlier Ayr second brings her into it
runners_data.spotlight: Her losing run stands at 18 and she disappointed as favourite at Beverley two weeks ago; on the plus side, she went desperately close at Ayr (behind Starliner) three weeks ago and won't be far away if back at that level.

runners_data.name: Barley
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse operating off reduced mark with encouraging signs last time, another 3lb drop helps his cause
runners_data.comment: More encouragement dropped to a Class 5 latest; dangerous mark; place claims
runners_data.spotlight: Not a prolific winner but he is operating off a reduced mark and there were more encouraging signs dropped to a Class 5 at Thirsk 11 days ago; another 3lb lower today and minor money could be on the cards.

runners_data.name: Sanafi Zabeel
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with German form who has shown promise in two Hamilton runs, Paul Mulrennan booking looks significant
runners_data.comment: 1m1f winner in Germany; two encouraging runs for new yard; Paul Mulrennan takes over today
runners_data.spotlight: 1m1f winner in Germany; enough promise in his two course runs for his new stable to think he would be winning sooner rather than later; Paul Mulrennan takes over today; interesting.

runners_data.name: Eve's Boy
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who was good on seasonal return but disappointed when favourite at Ayr, needs to bounce back
runners_data.comment: Promising 2nd on seasonal return but behind two of these at Ayr latest; headgear back now
runners_data.spotlight: Good second at Thirsk on his seasonal return last month; sent off favourite at Ayr on the strength of it but could only manage sixth of the seven runners behind Starliner (Donna Nook second); cheekpieces return.

runners_data.name: Yaaser
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 110-day break, smooth Newcastle winner in December but poor form since
runners_data.comment: Struggled since his AW win in December (7f); good mark but too much to prove
runners_data.spotlight: Smooth win at Newcastle (7f) in December and now rated 2lb lower; that is a result of beating just one horse home in four subsequent starts; jury out for now.

runners_data.name: Starliner
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who took advantage of career-low mark to beat Donna Nook at Ayr but disappointed at Thirsk last time
runners_data.comment: Beat two of these at Ayr three weeks ago but failed to fire at Thirsk last time; not solid
runners_data.spotlight: Took advantage of his career-low mark when beating Donna Nook at Ayr (1m, good to firm) three weeks ago; not so good at Thirsk last time and he is not the easiest to predict.

runners_data.name: Union Island
runners_data.note: Prominent runner in good form with two wins from last five starts, 2lb rise after Leicester success looks manageable
runners_data.comment: Eight-time winner, including two this year; conditions should suit; still feasibly treated
runners_data.spotlight: Won two of his last five starts (with and without headgear), scrambling home at Leicester (1m, good to firm) 18 days ago; a 2lb rise not excessive and he has a good strike-rate for one of his rating; chance.

races.paceDynamic: Donna Nook and Sanafi Zabeel will likely lead or track the pace from the outset, with Union Island also happy to race prominently in this small field. With only one confirmed front-runner and several hold-up horses, the early gallop should be manageable rather than fierce. The pace will gradually build through the middle stages before quickening in the final three furlongs. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers and those with tactical speed who can position close to the pace, as the hold-up horses may find too few to pass in such a small field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace Suits Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If Donna Nook and Sanafi Zabeel set a steady rhythm without pressure
scenarios.body: The pace-setters get an easy lead and kick clear when the tempo lifts, making it difficult for the hold-up horses to close the gap in time. The prominent runners have positional advantage and tactical speed when it matters.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Rally
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes moderate to slow and the field bunches up
scenarios.body: Starliner, Yaaser and Eve's Boy get the perfect setup to unleash their finishing kicks from off the pace. The race becomes a sprint finish where class and turn of foot matter most over positioning.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Gets Away
scenarios.trigger: If Donna Nook or Sanafi Zabeel steal a march and open up a decisive lead
scenarios.body: The leader builds an unassailable advantage as the small field fails to respond quickly enough to the injection of pace. Late challengers run out of ground despite staying on strongly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Tactical Affair
scenarios.trigger: If no horse wants to make the running early and the pace crawls
scenarios.body: The race becomes a stop-start affair with horses getting in each other's way, leading to a chaotic sprint finish. Jockey tactics and traffic luck become decisive factors over pure ability.

watchPoints.text: Donna Nook's 18-race losing sequence suggests confidence issues despite her class advantage
Yaaser returning from 110-day layoff with only poor form to recommend him recently
Sanafi Zabeel's German form and promising Hamilton runs make him interesting for Jim Goldie
Small field of seven may not provide enough pace or horses to pass for the hold-up runners
Paul Mulrennan taking over on Sanafi Zabeel suggests stable confidence in improvement
